title: Tier 2 nullifier key resharing: transcripts, reshared shares, their checks, key_id and approvals
generator: packages/crypto/scripts/nullifier-reshare-vectors.py: an independent Python implementation (standard library only) on nullifier-key-vectors.py's, and through it keyed-nullifier-vectors.py's Baby Jubjub, share-encryption-vectors.py's ML-KEM-768 and ChaCha20-Poly1305, group-vectors.py's ristretto255 and trustee-vectors.py's P-256 ECDSA, each checked against published vectors first. Every value is test data, never keys

transcripts.description: Seats 1 to 3 of the predecessor's 2-of-4 panel reshare to a new 3-of-4 panel; every new seat qualifies.
Only seats 1 and 3 deal, the predecessor's threshold: the new shares still give sk.
Seats 2 and 3 reshare to the predecessor's own panel: seat 4, absent from the predecessor, now holds a share.
New seat 2 sends nothing; the other three qualify.

Dealer 2 seals a wrong share to new seat 2 (share-verify) and one that doesn't open to new seat 4 (share-decrypt), and signs both hashes; both complain and dealer 2 reveals both shares correctly, so it stays qualified.
As complaint-answered, but dealer 2 reveals a wrong share for new seat 2.
As complaint-answered, but dealer 2 sends no round-4 message.
New seat 3 complains about honest dealer 1 without cause: dealer 1 reveals seat 3's own share, which checks.
Dealer 3 reshares something other than its own share: B_{3,0} isn't C_3, and the other two dealers carry the key.
Dealers 1 and 3 only, and dealer 3 reshares something other than its share: one qualified dealer, below k = 2.
New seat 4's signing-key signature is made by seat 1's signing key.
In a refresh, new seat 1 registers the signing key its seat registered for the predecessor.
New seat 3 registers the old panel's seat 1 identity key as its signing key.
Only new seats 1 and 2 take part: two qualified seats, below k' = 3.
The transcript names another predecessor.
Old seat 4, which holds no share of the predecessor, deals as well (signed under its identity key).
New seat 2, absent from round 1, complains about dealer 1 in round 3.
Dealer 1 omits its hash for the last new seat (signed as sent).
Dealer 1's round-2 message is signed by the new panel's seat 1 instead of the old panel's.
The run identifier is changed: every message was signed under the original context.
